```json
  "petitioner_position": "M&K Employee Solutions argues that pension funds cannot retroactively alter the actuarial interest rate assumptions used to calculate withdrawal liability after an employer has already withdrawn, as such retroactive changes result in significant miscalculations of withdrawal liability amounts — potentially by several million dollars — and violate established legal principles confirmed by the Second Circuit in Metz and affirmed by two separate arbitration proceedings; employers must be able to rely on the assumptions in place at the time of withdrawal to ensure predictability and fairness in withdrawal liability assessments.",

  "key_precedents": [
    "Metz v. [IAM National Pension Fund] (Second Circuit) — held that pension funds cannot retroactively alter interest rate assumptions used to calculate withdrawal liability",
    "Jacobson v. Fireman's Fund Insurance Co., 111 F.3d (2d Cir. 1997) — cited by the Fund in support of its position on summary judgment",
    "Two separate arbitration decisions rejecting the Fund's methodology for calculating M&K's withdrawal liability"
  ],
  "legal_complexity": "Complex"
}
```
